description: Wave 9 Security Hardening, SLA Compliance & Chaos Fault Tolerance Performance Gates.

hard_gates.description: Concurrent audit log write throughput must sustain ≥ 100 000 ops/s.
hard_gates.rationale: Audit logging is on the hot write path in security-hardened deployments; below 100 k ops/s, write-heavy workloads lose audit coverage under peak load.

hard_gates.description: Auth token validation p99 must not exceed 150 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: Auth validation is on every request path; p99 > 150 µs adds perceptible latency to interactive workloads and violates the W9 auth SLA.

hard_gates.description: Node restart and cluster rejoin cycle must complete within 2000 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: RTO for a single-node restart must be under 2 ms for the cluster to maintain quorum without client-visible disruption.

hard_gates.description: RTO simulation recovery cycle must complete within 5 000 µs (5 ms).
hard_gates.rationale: SLA contract requires recovery within 3 cycles; each cycle must stay under 5 ms to meet the overall RTO budget.

hard_gates.description: Multi-tenant isolation gate self-check must report triage_completeness = 1.0.
hard_gates.rationale: Benchmarks without gate_passed counters produce no CI signal; 100% coverage required for all W9 gate IDs.

hard_gates.description: Multi-tenant concurrent write throughput must sustain ≥ 60 000 ops/s.
hard_gates.rationale: Cross-tenant write throughput floor ensures that tenant-namespace overhead does not degrade write performance beyond the W9 SLA threshold.

soft_gates.description: p99 latency measurement CV should stay below 5%.
soft_gates.rationale: High CV in the p99 estimator masks real SLA compliance signals.

soft_gates.description: Write-storm completion time must not drift more than 8% across repetitions.
soft_gates.rationale: High variance in write-storm completion indicates scheduling or lock-contention instability.

soft_gates.description: Nonce store must produce zero false-negative lookups.
soft_gates.rationale: Any false negative in the nonce store would allow a replay attack to succeed.

known_limitations: SOA-01 auth validation uses an in-process FNV-1a hash rather than a real HMAC; production values will differ when a hardware crypto accelerator is in use.
SMC-04 RTO simulation uses logical step counts, not wall-clock time; actual recovery latency depends on network and disk I/O not captured here.
CFR-04 node rejoin uses in-process map copy; real rejoin involves WAL replay and network handshake not captured in this benchmark.
MTI-07 concurrent writes use a std::mutex-guarded map; production isolation may use separate RocksDB column families with different contention characteristics.
MTI-08 triage_completeness of 1.0 is asserted by count; tooling must verify each benchmark executable at release time.
